summary.headline: J. Kumar FY26 revenue rose 1% to INR5,723 crore with EBITDA flat at INR823 crore; management guides 15% top-line growth in FY27.
summary.overview: FY26 was a flat year: consolidated revenue rose 1% to INR5,723 crore, EBITDA was INR823 crore (14.4% margin) and PAT was INR387 crore, with management attributing the slowdown to external factors that delayed execution. Q4 FY26 revenue fell 3% YoY to INR1,585 crore and PAT fell 5% to INR110 crore. Order book stood at INR18,554 crore on 31 March 2026, and management says inflows since 1 April 2026 have taken it to about INR25,000 crore including L1. Management guides FY27 revenue and PAT growth of about 15%, EBITDA margin of 15-16%, and new order intake of INR9,000-10,000 crore.

financial_highlights.value: Unbilled revenue INR578 crore; mobilisation advance INR706 crore; retention INR464 crore

segments.name: Order book mix (31 March 2026)
segments.commentary: Elevated corridors and flyovers about 51%, others about 20%, road and tunnel projects about 18%, metro (elevated and underground) about 11%.

segments.name: Chennai and GMLR projects
segments.commentary: Chennai casting yard fully operational and segment casting started; GMLR has cast over 3.5 km of tunnel, and management expects roughly 20-30% output from Chennai and GMLR in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth about 15%, implying crossing INR6,500 crore; management says upside is possible but is committing to 15%.
FY27 PAT growth about 15%; PAT margin about 7%.
EBITDA margin targeted to rise from 14-15% to 15-16%, with further basis-point gains over 6-8 quarters.
FY27 new order intake target INR9,000-10,000 crore; management says it will cross INR10,000 crore, with INR15,000-20,000 crore of projects to bid in FY27.
Capex of INR200-250 crore per year for FY27 and FY28 including incremental capex and GMLR/Chennai balance.
Management says it is 'one year behind' its earlier INR7,500 crore FY27 revenue target (given when the dollar was INR75) and now expects it in FY28.
capex_capacity: Capex of about INR280 crore in FY25 and about INR400 crore in FY26; quarterly depreciation rose to about INR66 crore in Q4 FY26 from INR40-45 crore, and management expects it to stay elevated.

GMLR: TBM assembled; first machine in advanced assembly with SAT targeted around June 2026 and drilling to start then; second TBM about 1.5 months behind. The TBM is financed by a 3-year term loan, about 10% repaid so far, and no major additional TBM capex is planned.
Chennai: foundation and substructure work underway, casting yard operational. Management says the INR500 crore Chennai flyover project is about 50% complete and on schedule.

Versova-Dahisar Coastal Road Package B: approvals largely received, mangrove cutting about 10% done, over 100 piles and 14-15 foundations completed, 7-8 piers cast; a 6-7 km connector toward Filmcity is also in scope.
Vizag investment property (originally a PSL asset): INR90 crore of INR106 crore loan repaid; management expects the balance to be exited by Q2.
demand_pricing: Inflows since 1 April 2026 to 19 May 2026 about INR6,300 crore (LOA about INR4,500 crore, L1 about INR1,770 crore; L1 expected to convert in 15-30 days). Order book is about INR25,000 crore including these, versus INR18,554 crore at 31 March.

Maharashtra pipeline: Metro Lines 5, 10, 13 and 14, Uttan-Virar elevated corridor (over INR50,000-60,000 crore), tenders expected in 3-6 months. Management cites about INR1 lakh crore of Maharashtra awards expected within about 12 months.
Management says it deliberately did not bid at low margins in FY25 and FY26 (order inflow about INR2,500 crore and about INR1,000 crore), and says current orders are at target margins.

Pricing: contracts carry price variation and escalation clauses covering steel, cement, POL and labour, so management reports no margin impact from commodity or geopolitical moves; escalation is billed monthly.
Labour: site labour shortage of about 10-15% attributed to April-May elections and seasonal migration; management calls it temporary.
Management says the company bid INR11,000 crore in 2024 and that it could bid up to INR20,000 crore if an opportunity arises.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current bid pipeline and FY27 order book expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inflows of about INR6,300 crore so far, with FY27 order intake expected at INR9,000-10,000 crore and INR15,000-20,000 crore of projects to bid in the year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: About 15% revenue and PAT growth, with revenue crossing INR6,500 crore; EBITDA margin targeted at 15-16% from 14-15% and PAT margin around 7%.

qa_highlights.question: Does geopolitics, labour shortage or commodity prices affect execution and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no impact from geopolitics, with commodity risk passed through via escalation clauses; a 10-15% labour shortage is seasonal and temporary.

qa_highlights.question: Is depreciation going to keep rising, and how will TBM costs affect the P&L?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation will stay elevated; management said the TBM is costed into the project and it targets amortisation over about 3 years, though books will follow applicable rates.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the FY27 inflow target only INR10,000 crore given large opportunities?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is being realistic after two weak years and that it can cross INR10,000 crore, with capacity to bid larger amounts if opportunities arise.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company pursue buybacks given its net cash position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a buyback is on the agenda and was discussed by the Board, but dividends were paid this year; it will revisit later.

risks_watch: Order inflow depends on Maharashtra metro and elevated corridor tenders that have repeatedly slipped; FY27 inflow target is INR9,000-10,000 crore against about INR4,500 crore of LOA plus L1 of about INR1,770 crore.
Q4 FY26 margin fell about 30 bps YoY and revenue declined 3%; the 15% FY27 growth needs a sharp H2 ramp, with management not committing on Q1.
Depreciation run-rate of about INR65-66 crore per quarter and TBM loan repayments add to costs.
Labour availability (10-15% shortfall) and the timing of the first TBM drilling (around June 2026).
Governance: the Board has discussed a buyback versus dividend, and management referred to a $1 billion revenue target from August 2024 that it now says is one year behind schedule.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order momentum and margins, but guarded on volumes: management repeatedly declined to go beyond 15% growth and INR10,000 crore inflows, and explained past misses by external factors. Answers on TBM costs, the $1 billion target and the Chennai flyover were brief or deflected.
key_quotes: So this year, we are expecting a growth of around 15% in the top line.
It was a well-chosen thing that we don't want to book orders where we don't have good bottom line.
So there is no impact when I say for the contracts which are on EPC basis having price variation and escalation clauses.
But I'm sure that we'll be able to cross this INR10,000 mark even this year.

growth.why: Management guides about 15% FY27 revenue growth (above INR6,500 crore) and 15-16% EBITDA margin, backed by an order book of about INR18,554 crore at 31 March (about INR25,000 crore including L1) and Chennai/GMLR ramp-up expected to contribute 20-30% of output in FY27, though no specific capacity additions with numbers were quantified beyond TBM and yard timelines.
